We decided to go to another clinic, and the vet there gave our cat a completely different treatment. Turns out, it wasn’t a rare disease, and the medication was not difficult to find. They also explained why their treatment approach differed from the original and that if we had gone through with the first procedure, it could have worsened the symptoms and even led to death. We were so relieved that we left that place in time.

We recently took our dog to be spayed. She's very small and has delicate skin, so when we removed the plaster from her belly wound, she cried so pitifully. We spent a long time treating her wound at home because we were afraid of causing her pain. One day, we couldn't bear to see her in so much pain anymore. So, we drove from our home in Samut Prakan to the vet in Rama 9, a very long distance. We arrived late at night and saw Dr. Tawan, the doctor on duty. Our first reaction was that he was very emotional when talking to his assistants. Both assistants seemed terrified of him, even though they were very gentle and kind to our dog. As soon as we handed our little dog to Dr. Tawan, he told us that the easy way was to just apply alcohol to the plaster and peel it off. Immediately after saying that, he violently yanked the plaster off. Our dog screamed, her belly was red and scraped. We were furious but didn't want to cause a scene. He acted like he knew everything, completely lacking the ethics and compassion of a good veterinarian. We were extremely disappointed. After that, our dog became afraid of everyone. Even with us, he's wary. We really can't forgive this vet. Regarding the perfect score and 5-star ratings given by customers on Google Maps, we want you to know that the hospital stated that if you give 5 stars, they will give you a discount on the treatment cost. That is probably the reason why the score is good.

One day, I couldn't bear to do it myself anymore because seeing him in pain was too much. I decided to drive all the way from my home in Samut Prakan to a hospital in Rama 9. Despite the long distance, I went in the middle of the night and met Dr. Tawan, who was the on-call veterinarian that shift.
The first thing I noticed was how he spoke to his assistants; he seemed very temperamental and emotional. The two staff members looked terrified of him, even though they were being very gentle and sweet with my dog.
As soon as I handed my little dog to Dr. Tawan, he told me that the 'simple' way to do it was to just apply alcohol over the plaster and peel it off. While he was saying this, he suddenly yanked the bandage off with great force—I emphasize, he ripped it off violently. My dog ​​screamed in pain. His belly was bright red and Cooper had visible abrasions.
I was furious, but I didn't want to start an altercation. He acted like a 'full cup' (arrogant and unwilling to listen), showing a complete lack of professional ethics and no mercy or gentleness toward animals. I was deeply disappointed.
Since that incident, my dog ​​has become terrified of everyone. He is even suspicious and paranoid around me. I truly cannot forgive this doctor. Regarding the 5-star reviews on Google Maps, I want people to know that the hospital offers discounts on treatment in exchange for 5-star ratings. That is likely why their score remains so high.
